chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! How did it come to be that when a man dies and his children are of the same kinship (equal in relation), the women inherit half the inheritance of the men, while they are weaker than the men and have less capability?' So he said: 'Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, preferred the men over the women by a degree, and because the women return to be dependents upon the men.'
ai.seo_question: Why do daughters inherit half the share of sons in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the wisdom behind the 2:1 inheritance ratio by linking it to the divine preference for men and the corresponding financial burden of *nafaqah* (maintenance) borne by males. This explanation, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the Shia scholarly view that the disparity in shares is not a reflection of inferiority but rather a compensation for the exclusive duty of financial provision, thereby balancing the rights and responsibilities within the family structure.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>,

(the narrator says) ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! How did it come to be such that when the man dies and his children are all equal in the relationship, (but) the women (the daughters of the deceased) inherit half the inheritance of the men (sons of the deceased), and they (women) are weaker than the men, and of less capabilities?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Preferred the men over the women with a level, and because the women return for the dependency upon the men’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Isma‘il ibn Marrar from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman who has narrated the following: “I once asked al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, why is it that when a man dies his sons’ shares of the legacy are twice as much as the share of his daughters even though females are less capable and weaker?’
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has preferred men over women and because women become dependents of men.’”
